patients.label: 54-year-old male with basal cell carcinoma of the right nasal ala and a prior paramedian forehead flap, treated with resection and flap with tubular skin graft lining

identity_evidence.quote: We present the case of a 54-year-old male

attribution_limitations: The graft donor site is stated as retroauricular in the abstract, case text and one Case presentation sentence but as preauricular in the Conclusions.

The article title calls the carcinoma recurrent, but the case text does not label the current lesion as a recurrence; it describes a history of basal cell carcinoma treated six months earlier with positive margins.
The side of the prior flap and of the sacrificed supratrochlear artery is described only as contralateral, with no stated reference side or left or right.
The tumor subtype is described as infiltrative solid-type (diagnosis) and as clinically suggestive of nodular-ulcerative (morphology).
The anterior rhinoscopy result is not stated, and the timing of the NOSE assessment is not stated.
The reconstructed region is called the nasal vestibule in the text and the nasal antrum or antral defect elsewhere.

claims.text: A 54-year-old male attended the clinic with infiltrative solid-type basal cell carcinoma of the right nasal ala, confirmed as malignant. The same site had been treated six months earlier with resection and a paramedian forehead flap, with positive margins. History included tobacco and alcohol use, type 2 diabetes, hypertension and HIV with undetectable viral load. The lesion, approximately 10x15 mm, was pearly and ulcerated with telangiectasias, clinically highly suggestive of nodular-ulcerative basal cell carcinoma.

claims.text: The right nasal ala and vestibule were resected and the defect was covered with a paramedian forehead flap with a vertical pedicle about 2 cm wide, the contralateral side being unavailable because the supratrochlear artery was sacrificed in the prior procedure. A full-thickness skin graft was fashioned into a tubular structure, sutured to the nasal vestibule mucosa as mucosal lining, and the flap was opened to let it cover the new nostril. Cotton in a glove finger supported the nostril; cartilage harvest was not required.
